prompt.context_jp: 蒲田支店の営業室に、朝から重苦しい空気＿張り詰めていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 蒲田支店の営業室に、朝から重苦しい空気＿張り詰めていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits the opening scene description.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence introduces a new scene — the heavy atmosphere is new information presented to the reader, so が marks it.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat 空気 as an already-established topic, but here the atmosphere is being introduced for the first time.

contrast_examples.en: There is a cat in the room. (new info)

prompt.context_jp: 門脇課長＿気づいて 処理を止めてくれたから すんでのところで 大事に至らずに済んだ
prompt.prompt_jp: 門脇課長＿気づいて 処理を止めてくれたから…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits Suga's praise of Kadowaki?

feedback.correct_en: Suga is identifying specifically WHO noticed — exhaustive-listing が highlights Kadowaki as the one who caught the error.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply Kadowaki is already the topic under discussion, but here he's being singled out as the hero of the moment.

prompt.context_jp: 回線の先で応じたの＿、本部の児玉直樹であった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 回線の先で応じたの＿、本部の児玉直樹であった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this cleft construction?

feedback.correct_en: The nominalized clause 'the one who answered' is the topic, and 児玉 is the identifying predicate — the Xのは Y だ cleft pattern requires は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the clause the subject of some other predicate; the cleft 'the one who X is Y' needs のは.

contrast_examples.en: The one who came is Tanaka.

prompt.context_jp: 須賀にとって花咲を陥れる小細工＿、上への忠誠を示す絶好の一手にほかならなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 須賀にとって花咲を陥れる小細工＿、上への忠誠を示す絶好の一手にほかならなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: The scheme is set up as the topic being characterized ('as for the scheme, it was nothing but...'). は marks the topic of this definitional statement.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce it as new information, but the sentence is explaining what the scheme MEANS to Suga — a topic-comment structure.

prompt.context_jp: わざとやったのよ 花咲さん＿失敗するように
prompt.prompt_jp: わざとやったのよ 花咲さん＿失敗するように
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this subordinate clause?

feedback.correct_en: In a subordinate clause (〜ように), the embedded subject takes が. は tends to escape to mark the main-clause topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside a 〜ように clause would sound unnatural — subordinate clauses in Japanese typically use が for their subject.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が来るように頼んだ。
contrast_examples.en: I asked so that he would come.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は来るように頼まれた。
contrast_examples.en: He was asked to come. (main topic)

prompt.context_jp: 蒲田支店の業績＿下がってるのは 間違いなく 須賀支店長のせいだろうな
prompt.prompt_jp: 蒲田支店の業績＿下がってるのは 間違いなく 須賀支店長のせいだろうな
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this nominalized clause?

feedback.correct_en: Inside the のは nominalization ('the fact that performance is declining'), the embedded subject takes が. The main-clause は is already used on のは.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside a relative/nominalized clause is blocked here because the のは cleft already carries the topic marking.

contrast_examples.en: As for him, his coming is rare. (awkward)

prompt.context_jp: 隣の卓で杯を傾けていた常連客＿、しびれを切らしたように口を挟んだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 隣の卓で杯を傾けていた常連客＿、しびれを切らしたように口を挟んだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces this new character?

feedback.correct_en: The regular customer is being introduced for the first time — が marks this new participant entering the scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply this customer was already an established topic in the conversation, but he's just appearing now.

contrast_examples.jp: 知らない人が入ってきた。
その人は常連客だった。
contrast_examples.en: That person was a regular. (now topic)

prompt.context_jp: この口座に登録されている名前＿ "荒磯の子"ではなく "新井園子"なんです
prompt.prompt_jp: この口座に登録されている名前＿ "荒磯の子"ではなく "新井園子"なんです
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: Mai is making the registered name the topic and then identifying what it actually is — 'As for the name, it's X not Y.' Topic は fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce the name as new info, but she's drawing attention to the known entity and clarifying its identity — a classic topic-comment move.

prompt.context_jp: 息を切らせて飛び込んできたの＿、駆けつけたばかりの花咲舞であった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 息を切らせて飛び込んできたの＿、駆けつけたばかりの花咲舞であった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this cleft?

feedback.correct_en: This is the 'Xのは Y だ' cleft identifying who rushed in — the nominalized clause must take は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 'the one who rushed in' act as subject of some further predicate, but here it's the topic being identified as Mai.

prompt.context_jp: あんな詐欺なんかにダマされたの＿ 須賀支店長ですよね？
prompt.prompt_jp: あんな詐欺なんかにダマされたの＿ 須賀支店長ですよね？
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits Mai's accusation?

feedback.correct_en: Mai uses the のは cleft to contrastively identify WHO was fooled — pointing the finger directly at Suga, not the staff.
feedback.incorrect_en: が in the cleft slot doesn't work; the nominalized subject needs は, which also carries the contrastive 'it was HIM, not us' force.

contrast_examples.en: The one at fault is YOU.

prompt.context_jp: この支店に必要ないの＿ 須賀支店長 あなたです！
prompt.prompt_jp: この支店に必要ないの＿ 須賀支店長 あなたです！
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this climactic line?

feedback.correct_en: Mai throws Suga's own words back at him using the のは cleft to spotlight who's really unnecessary — contrastive は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が cannot occupy the nominalized topic slot before だ in this cleft; は is required and gives the contrastive punch.

contrast_examples.jp: いらないのはあなただ。
contrast_examples.en: The one who's not needed is YOU.

prompt.context_jp: しかし花咲の胸には、事件そのものとは別の憤り＿燻り続けていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: しかし花咲の胸には、事件そのものとは別の憤り＿燻り続けていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: A separate anger is newly introduced as something that exists in Mai's heart — が marks this new entity being presented.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would require this anger to already be a known topic; here the narrator is introducing it for the first time.

contrast_examples.en: There is anxiety in my heart. (existence)

prompt.context_jp: 叱責の余韻がなお漂う営業室の隅で、花咲＿同僚たちに深く頭を下げていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 花咲＿同僚たちに深く頭を下げていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for the already-known main character?

feedback.correct_en: Hanasaki is the established protagonist — は keeps her as the ongoing topic in this descriptive scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would re-introduce her as new info, which clashes with her being the known protagonist of the chapter.

prompt.context_jp: 須賀と門脇の顔には、大口案件をまとめた安堵の色＿浮かんでいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 須賀と門脇の顔には、大口案件をまとめた安堵の色＿浮かんでいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: The look of relief appears on their faces — a newly observed thing, so が marks it as new perceptual information.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat 安堵の色 as a prior topic, but it's being introduced as what's visible on their faces now.

contrast_examples.en: A smile appears on the face.

prompt.context_jp: 君に入金＿依頼したのは "株式会社 明石ビルディング"
prompt.prompt_jp: 君に入金＿依頼したのは "株式会社 明石ビルディング"
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the direct object?

feedback.correct_en: 依頼する takes を to mark what is being requested — the deposit is the object of the request.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 入金 a subject (wrong — it's what's being requested); に would mark a destination/recipient, but 君に already fills that slot.

prompt.context_jp: 翌朝、臨店部の部屋＿出勤した花咲は、通帳の名義照合を終えて席を立った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 翌朝、臨店部の部屋＿出勤した花咲は…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the destination of coming to work?

feedback.correct_en: 出勤する means 'to go to/arrive at work' — に marks the destination of arrival.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark a location of ongoing action; を would mark a path. For arrival at a workplace, に is correct.

prompt.context_jp: フッ… まったく ＿＿ 入金先を間違えるなんて 新人でもしないミスだ
prompt.prompt_jp: まったく ＿＿ 入金先を間違えるなんて
prompt.prompt_en: Which expression fits Suga's contemptuous remark?

feedback.correct_en: ざまはない is a harsh, mocking expression meaning 'what a pathetic sight' — matches Suga's contemptuous tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: しかたない ('can't be helped') is sympathetic; もったいない ('wasteful') doesn't match the context of mocking a mistake.

prompt.context_jp: アア… ＿＿ハメられましたよ だから あんな勝ち誇ったような顔してたんですよね
prompt.prompt_jp: アア… ＿＿ハメられましたよ
prompt.prompt_en: Which adverb best fits 'completely set up'?

feedback.correct_en: まんまと means 'completely/skillfully (tricked)' — it collocates specifically with being fooled or deceived.
feedback.incorrect_en: そろそろ ('soon') and ぼちぼち ('gradually') have nothing to do with being tricked; they don't fit the frustration here.

prompt.context_jp: ＿＿＿＿＿と言うように、こうした小さな貸しの積み重ねこそが、いずれ自らの出世を後押しすると信じて疑わないのだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: ＿＿＿＿＿と言うように、こうした小さな貸しの積み重ねこそが…
prompt.prompt_en: Which proverb fits here?

choices.text: 塵も積もれば山となる

feedback.correct_en: 塵も積もれば山となる ('even dust piled up becomes a mountain') perfectly matches the idea of small favors accumulating into career advancement.
feedback.incorrect_en: 猿も木から落ちる is about even experts failing; 急がば回れ is 'haste makes waste' — neither fits the theme of accumulation.

contrast_examples.jp: 塵も積もれば山となる。
contrast_examples.en: Many a little makes a mickle.

prompt.context_jp: いや 苦情＿＿でネットでは結構 前から ウワサになってた
prompt.prompt_jp: 苦情＿＿でネットでは結構 前からウワサになってた
prompt.prompt_en: Which word means 'flooding in'?

feedback.correct_en: 殺到(さっとう) means 'rush/flood in' and collocates perfectly with 苦情 ('complaints pouring in').
feedback.incorrect_en: 到着 means 'arrival' (singular, neutral) and 到達 means 'reaching'; neither captures the overwhelming flood of complaints.

prompt.context_jp: ＿＿＿＿＿＿＿＿ようですが… ここにいる人たちは みんな 無能なヤツらではありません！
prompt.prompt_en: Which polite phrase introduces a respectful disagreement?

feedback.correct_en: お言葉を返すようですが is a set phrase used to politely push back against a superior — exactly Mai's stance against Suga.
feedback.incorrect_en: お手数をかける ('to trouble someone') and お世話になる ('to be indebted') are courtesies, not disagreement openers.

contrast_examples.jp: お言葉を返すようですが、違います。
お手数をおかけします。

prompt.context_jp: まあ あの課長が独断で そんなことできるわけないから 支店長の＿＿＿だろうね
prompt.prompt_jp: 支店長の＿＿＿だろうね
prompt.prompt_en: Which word means 'behind-the-scenes manipulation'?

feedback.correct_en: 差し金(さしがね) refers to someone secretly pulling the strings — fits the implication that Suga ordered Kadowaki.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手料理 ('home cooking') and 手続き ('procedure') don't fit — neither implies manipulation from behind.

contrast_examples.en: It's the boss's doing (behind the scenes).

prompt.context_jp: 他人名義の口座ですとか 存在しない人の名前を使って 銀行を＿＿＿て 作った口座のことです
prompt.prompt_jp: 銀行を＿＿＿て 作った口座のことです
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb means 'to deceive'?

feedback.correct_en: 銀行をダマす means 'to deceive the bank' — exactly how fake accounts are opened.
feedback.incorrect_en: タノしむ ('enjoy') takes を but doesn't fit; ハタラく ('work') is intransitive and doesn't collocate.

prompt.context_jp: Suga is scolding Mai in a formal workplace setting.
prompt.prompt_en: Which apology fits a subordinate addressing a boss in a bank setting?

choices.text: 申し訳ありませんでした

feedback.correct_en: 申し訳ありませんでした is the standard formal apology to a superior in a business setting — the form Mai uses throughout the scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: ごめんね is casual (to friends/family); 悪かった is also informal and would sound insubordinate to a branch manager.

contrast_examples.jp: 申し訳ありませんでした。

prompt.context_jp: Suga is boasting to Kodama by phone that he humiliated Mai as promised.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural for Suga's smug boast?

choices.text: お約束どおり こてんぱんにしてやりましたよ
約束のとおりに とてもひどくしましたよ
約束したから めちゃくちゃにさせましたよ

feedback.correct_en: こてんぱんにする is the natural idiom for 'thoroughly crushing' someone, and お約束どおり is the standard business-phone register for 'as promised.'
feedback.incorrect_en: B and C use clumsy paraphrases that lack the idiomatic punch Suga's gloating needs; they sound unnatural in a phone-boast register.

contrast_examples.jp: こてんぱんにやられた。
約束どおりやりました。

prompt.context_jp: Mai complains about how working under Suga would destroy anyone's motivation.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing of 'motivation plummets' sounds most natural?

choices.text: モチベーションだだ下がりですよ
モチベーションが低く降りますよ
モチベーションを下に落としますよ

feedback.correct_en: だだ下がり is a vivid colloquial compound meaning 'plummets uncontrollably' — exactly how Mai talks and natural with モチベーション.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses 降りる (physical descent) which doesn't collocate with motivation; C's を落とす construction sounds translated and unnatural.

prompt.context_jp: Souma warns Mai about getting too emotionally invested in branch employees.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural as Souma's warning?

choices.text: そこまで毎回 支店の行員に肩入れしてたら この先 臨店の仕事やってくの 大変だぞ
そこまで毎回 支店の行員に味方してあげたら この先 臨店の仕事するの つらいぞ
そこまで毎回 支店の行員の肩を持ち上げたら この先 臨店の仕事やるの 困難だぞ

feedback.correct_en: 肩入れする is the idiomatic verb for 'siding with/backing someone', and 大変だぞ matches Souma's gruff mentor tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: B's 味方してあげる sounds childish; C's 肩を持ち上げる is a literal mash-up that isn't a real idiom (the real one is 肩を持つ).

prompt.context_jp: Souma realizes how the katakana trick fooled victims.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural?

choices.text: 同じ読み方でも 個人名ならば 振込先として怪しいが これなら 会社名に見える
同じ読み方でも 個人の名前なら 振込先として変だが これなら 会社の名前っぽい
読み方が同じでも 人の名前は 振り込みの先に 怪しくて これなら 会社の名前らしい

feedback.correct_en: Option A uses crisp, idiomatic Japanese: ならば, 怪しい, 会社名に見える — natural for Souma's analytical register.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is too casual (〜っぽい) for the moment; C has awkward word order and particle choices that sound unnatural.

prompt.context_jp: Suga snaps back at Mai, dismissing her as a mere rinten temp.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural for Suga's angry put-down?

choices.text: 臨店ごときが 生意気な口をたたくな！
臨店みたいな人が 生意気な口を使うな！
臨店なんかの人が 生意気な口を話すな！

feedback.correct_en: ごとき is the condescending particle meaning 'the likes of', and 口をたたく is the natural idiom for 'to run one's mouth'.
feedback.incorrect_en: B and C use wrong verbs (口を使う/話す aren't idioms) and softer phrasing (みたい/なんかの人) that undercut Suga's contemptuous tone.

contrast_examples.jp: お前ごときに負けるか。
contrast_examples.en: As if I'd lose to the likes of you.

contrast_examples.jp: 生意気な口をたたくな。
